final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor offered no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim to a caveated launch-readiness theory based on the same record. That reframing is useful, but it does not cure the policy defect. The admissible evidence still shows a 1.0-point miss in a named launch use case tied to two enterprise commitments, an open legal ticket on disclosure, and a policy requiring disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch for material limitations in named launch use cases. There is still no admissible evidence of disclosure, approved risk acceptance, amended commitments, or final legal clearance. A caveated description of the packet may be more accurate than an overbroad claim of full resolution, but compliant_with_caveats would require the caveat itself to satisfy the governing predicate or reduce it to a non-required matter. Here the caveat identifies an unresolved compliance predicate, so the record remains noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the named field-service dispatch limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering this named launch use case before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open with no final answer.
The affected segment is tied to two enterprise deployment commitments, so product's non-core characterization does not resolve materiality under the policy.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness only; they do not satisfy the separate disclosure or risk-acceptance predicate.
